title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core go-to-market assets for prospect conversations: positioning and messaging, competitive briefs and battlecards, recommended pitch-deck structure, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document as the canonical source for standard responses, slide templates, and objection handling.

Audience: AEs, SDRs, SEs, solutions engineers, product marketing, and customer success.

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: Go-to-market (Maya Patel)
- Review cadence: quarterly or on major product/pricing/controls changes
- Living assets: slides, competitive matrix, and case study anonymized data live in the Sales Drive folder (link in related_pages)

1) Positioning and core messaging

Elevator pitch (30s):
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform that makes high-performance LLM inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We help engineering teams deliver fast, reliable model-powered experiences while controlling latency, cost, and operational risk.

Key value props (talking points by persona)
- For engineering teams:
  - Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private modes — one API, consistent behavior, and identical deployment primitives.
  - Production-first optimizations (continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, kernel selection) to meet strict latency targets while lowering per-token cost.
  - Observability and rollouts: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, canary and A/B deploys.
- For platform/infra teams:
  - Predictable capacity with Dedicated GPU pools and SLA options; smart routing to reduce cross-region blast radius.
  - Private deployments with VPC/on-prem options and KMS/HSM integrations for regulated workloads.
- For product/engineering leadership:
  - Clear unit economics: tooling to recommend batching, quantization, and caching profiles to optimize cost without sacrificing quality.

Proof points and metrics to use in conversations
- Typical production latency SLOs: 50–200ms median depending on model/sequence length (call out specific benchmark for agreed model)
- Cost reduction levers: intelligent batching + KV caching typically reduce per-token cost by 20–60% depending on workload
- Adoption signals: X customers on Dedicated (use up-to-date number from Sales Drive), SOC 2 Type II in process/completed (refer to security docs)

2) Competitive brief and battlecards

Top competitors to call out (short brief)
- Large public cloud AI endpoints (Competitor A): strong integration with cloud infra and marketplace positioning; weaker in unified private deployment and developer ergonomics for inference economics.
- LLM API providers (Competitor B): simple API and managed access; often proprietary black-box models, limited deployment modes, and less control over unit economics.
- Self-hosted inference runtimes (Competitor C): deep control and possible lower cost but require significant engineering investment to reach production reliability and observability parity.

Competitive matrix (high-level)
- Columns: "Deployment Modes", "Latency/Perf", "Cost Controls", "Observability", "Enterprise Security", "Ease of Onboarding"
- Redwood: "Hosted/Dedicated/Private", "High (runtime optimizations)", "Strong (batching, caching, quant profiles)", "Extensive (token-level)", "Enterprise (VPC, KMS, audit)", "Fast (developer-first API)"
- Competitor A: "Hosted/Dedicated", "Good", "Limited", "Basic", "Strong (cloud-native)", "Moderate"
- Competitor B: "Hosted only", "Variable", "Low", "Limited", "Limited", "Very easy"
- Competitor C: "Private/on-prem", "Variable (engineer-dependent)", "Potential", "Depends", "Customer-managed", "Slow (need infra)"

Battlecard — 60s rebuttals and prioritized objections
- Objection: "We can just use Cloud Provider X model endpoints."
  - Response: Cloud endpoints are fine for experimentation, but they offer limited control over inference economics and private deployment. Redwood provides predictable Dedicated capacity, VPC-private control plane, and tooling to reduce unit costs while preserving latency SLOs.
- Objection: "Self-hosting will be cheaper."
  - Response: Self-hosting often underestimates engineering and reliability overhead. Redwood's Dedicated and Private offerings accelerate time-to-production with SLA-backed capacity and operational tooling (rollouts, tracing, cost breakdowns) that reduce long-term TCO.
- Objection: "We're concerned about data residency and compliance."
  - Response: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem installs, KMS/HSM integration, and configurable retention policies; we also have SOC 2 evidence and compliance engagement playbooks. See Security FAQ.

3) Recommended pitch deck structure (10–12 slides)

Slide 1 — Title & TL;DR
Slide 2 — Customer pain and scale (metrics they care about)
Slide 3 — Product overview: deployment modes and key differentiators
Slide 4 — How it works (runtime, smart routing, caching, batch optimizations) — one diagram
Slide 5 — Performance & economics (benchmarks vs. alternatives)
Slide 6 — Security & compliance (VPC, KMS, audit logging, SOC2)
Slide 7 — Integration & rollout plan (API, SDKs, sample code, canary strategy)
Slide 8 — Pricing & recommended commercial model for customer scenario
Slide 9 — Case study / reference (similar customer outcomes)
Slide 10 — Proposed next steps & timeline (POC to production)

Deck tips and templates
- Use engineering-facing benchmarks only when agreed on model/seq-length.
- Include a short appendix with config examples (autoscaling, cache TTLs, quantization profiles).
- Provide a one-page technical handoff for SEs with CLI examples and key endpoints.

4) Pricing guidance and commercial patterns

Pricing philosophy: usage-based for Hosted to lower time-to-value; reserved capacity for Dedicated (committed monthly/annual); licensing + support for Private. Provide examples rather than firm quotes in early-stage conversations.

Common commercial patterns (with recommended talking points)
- Self-serve trial (hosted): "Start with a free credit-based trial to validate model and integration."
- POC to pilot (dedicated): recommend a 6-8 week pilot on a Dedicated pool with a scoped SLA and performance checkpoints. Typical pilot deliverables:
  1) Integration plan and ingest sample data
  2) Baseline benchmarks (latency/throughput) on agreed model and seq lengths
  3) Cost analysis and optimization recommendations (batching/quantization)
  4) Security and compliance checklist (VPC, KMS, retention)
- Enterprise: annual committed Dedicated with capacity ramp and runbook handoff; include premium support and onboarding credits.

Pricing conversation scripts (short)
- Early discovery: "Tell me about your expected throughput, peak qps, and latency goals. We typically recommend starting hosted for rapid validation, then move to Dedicated when you need predictable throughput or private networking."
- Cost objection: "We need a predictable cost model." — respond: "We offer reserved Dedicated SKUs with committed monthly/annual pricing and tooling to forecast token spend. We also provide recommendations (batching, caching, quant) to reduce per-token cost."

5) Case studies (representative, anonymized)

Case study A – 9: Customer type: AI-native SaaS; use case: real-time assistant for support agents; outcome: 3x reduction in median response latency and 35% lower inference spend after batching+cache.
Case study B – 9: Customer type: Enterprise fintech; use case: personalized summaries over protected data in a VPC; outcome: Successful Private deployment with KMS integration, met SOC 2 controls, and achieved 99.95% availability SLA during pilot.
Case study C – 9: Customer type: Marketplace startup; use case: semantic search and reranking at scale; outcome: reduced per-query cost by 45% after quantization profiles and model routing; throughput scaled to 2k qps on Dedicated pool.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers)

Q: What deployment modes do you support?
A: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private (VPC-hosted and on-prem options).

Q: How is customer data protected at rest and in transit?
A: TLS 1.2+/AES-GCM for in-transit, AES-256 for data at rest. Private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control.

Q: Do you retain customer data or model prompts?
A: By default, hosted logs are retained for 30 days for debugging and observability and can be configured per-customer. For Dedicated/Private, retention policies can be customer-managed; we support configurable TTLs and deletion APIs.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: SOC 2 Type II (in process/completed depending on customer date), and we provide artifacts and an engagement playbook for enterprise assessments.

Q: How do you support secure network isolation?
A: Private deployments are deployed inside the customer VPC or on-prem with private connectivity, security groups, and routing controls; control plane connectivity is optional and can be air-gapped for on-prem installs.

Q: How are keys managed?
A: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSMs for Private deployments; Dedicated customers can choose to enable CMKs for at-rest encryption.

Q: What logging and auditing is available?
A: Token-level cost and latency traces, request/response audit logs, admin action audit trails, and optional S3/event streaming of logs for retention.

Q: Do you allow subprocessor or third-party vendor audits?
A: Yes; we provide a standard questionnaire and can arrange SCAs under NDA for enterprise customers.
